claims.text: Introducing a heterostructured gradient nanostructure into a conventional alloy can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
A heterostructured gradient nanostructure enhances local strain partitioning.
Local strain partitioning can be detected by in-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction under controlled loading.
Traditional processing such as precipitation hardening or grain refinement produces a conventional alloy with a homogeneous microstructure.
The proposed processing creates spatially varying grain sizes or phase distributions.
Spatial gradients in grain size or phase distribution produce different local mechanical responses.
The microstructural gradient promotes local strain partitioning.
Local strain partitioning delays the onset of localized deformation.
The gradient activates multiple deformation mechanisms concurrently.
Concurrent deformation mechanisms enhance both strength and ductility relative to a homogeneous structure.
The gradient-structured material will exhibit statistically significant improvements in both strength and ductility.
In-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction will reveal clear local strain partitioning in the gradient-structured material.
Clear local strain partitioning will be absent from the conventional homogeneous alloy.
Traditional strengthening methods increase strength while reducing ductility in the baseline alloy.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on whether a given alloy system can reliably develop the desired gradient.
The effectiveness of the approach may be sensitive to the scale and uniformity of the heterostructure.
